chapter_title: Concerning the Sect of the Basket

fills.notes: The series here enumerates hypostases in descending order; after the tree/fruit correspondence the text pivots to the constitution of the cosmos. In the oldest Iranian substrate the immediate cosmic principle paired with Mind is Soul (life as the recipient-form of Mind).

A second ‘great’ preceding ‘great Mind’ is best read as the primal element/realm out of which Mind is manifest. ‘Light’ fits the substrate register (impersonal cosmological element) better than later ecclesial terms.

The clause ‘the great Mind that is … this Youth’ demands a participle linking Mind to its epiphanic form as ‘Youth’. ‘Revealed/manifest’ is the expected correspondential move: Mind in itself, then Mind in appearance.

The ‘Youth’ in Manichaean-cognate strata is the active demiurgic agent; in the oldest layer this corresponds to the Life-Spirit that orders forms. The surrounding angelic enumerations match the Living Spirit’s administration of the constructed cosmos.

‘This Youth … with the … thirty-six angels’ implies an intermediate cardinal group that, with 36, yields the common 12×3 structuring of powers/images elsewhere in the chapter. Twelve coheres with the later mention of ‘twelve powers’ and ‘twelve images’ as discrete degrees.
The syntax needs a verb/relative clause completing the first angelic cohort before introducing the next. The register is administrative/structural, not devotional.
Parallelism with the 36 suggests a second ordered cohort. The text is listing ranks supporting the cosmic architecture.
The phrase ‘but … of the twenty-two … the seven pillars’ strongly constrains the missing number to ‘seven’ as the extracted subset from the 22 that function architectonically as pillars.
Only the completion to ‘stand’ is required by the preserved letters and grammar (‘pillars that stan[d …]’).
‘the sea that surrounds the universe …’ expects an adverbial locator tied to the pillars and sea as boundary-supports. Old-layer cosmology treats the cosmic sea as the encircling limit.
The four angels ‘distributed to the … universe’ are typically at the four corners/quarters as stabilizers. This is correspondentially the extension of order into spatial ultimates.
Completes ‘supporting the mightiness … below’ with a pronominal object referring to the universe/disk just mentioned.
‘below, which is the earth of all the heavens’ reads as the foundational stratum. ‘Set/placed’ is the expected ontological verb in this register.
Introduces the ‘other five gods’ as a further tier in a stacked cosmography (over/above/beyond the lower supports).
‘they that … the universe is stood firm’ requires a constructive verb. The substrate describes stabilizing as building/establishing forms in ultimates.
Completes the passive sense: the universe ‘is stood firm’ by these agents/powers.
‘The third also, … below’ points to the third region/degree in a tripartite cosmography; ‘in the depth’ fits the descent into the lowest discrete degree.
Small locator needed to anchor ‘below, there are twelve powers standing firm there’.

The text immediately contrasts ‘twelve powers’ with ‘twelve images’ and then with ‘three great pillars’. Explaining twelve as 3×4 matches the chapter’s recurring triadic structuring into quarters (discrete degrees expressed in ultimates).
Grammatical completion: ‘the three great pillars of mightiness that … pillars supporting the disk’.
The passage distinguishes ‘three great pillars’ and then ‘the other three’; supplying ‘are three’ prepares the explicit parallel set.
Completes ‘pillars supporting the disk …’ with reference back to the disk/universe.

The ‘other three … they are the garments that the Living Spirit …’ requires naming the second triad before identifying them correspondentially as garments (outermost forms). ‘Glory’ keeps the impersonal radiance register of the oldest layer.
‘the garments that the Living Spirit … he put them at that time’ needs a verb of assumption before the act of putting/placing.
Where garments are ‘put’ in cosmological architecture is the visible expanse (firmament), i.e., ultimates where inner powers appear as outer form.
‘that threw them, together with … which is displayed therein’ implies the adversarial counterforce that ‘throws’ (projects) forms into mixture. In the substrate this is Darkness as active principle.
What is ‘displayed therein’ (in the firmament/world) is the mixed condition of light and darkness. This is the core cosmological datum of the oldest stratum.
After mixture the text points to ‘this … perfect before … great Porter’: the missing term is the ordering principle by which the mixture is held in form.
Small article before ‘great Porter’.
Article before the title phrase.
The line ‘perfect before … great Porter’ needs an identificatory clause introducing the title as a known cosmic function/name.
‘… great Porter … in his power’ requires an active description: the Porter stands/keeps watch at the boundary between degrees.
A ‘Porter’ implies gates. In correspondential cosmology gates are discrete-degree boundaries; the Porter is the function that regulates influx/efflux.

The concluding ‘these are the three great … against …’ loops back to identify the triad as defensive supports. Restoring ‘pillars of mightiness’ preserves the chapter’s internal terminology and ties to the ‘against’ clause (standing against dissolution/assault).

assessment: Only ¶3 is mechanically recoverable. ¶5–¶6 are heavily lacunose and preserve mainly the scaffold of an enumeration: ranks (Youth/Living Spirit), angelic cohorts, seven pillars, cosmic sea, four quarter-guardians, five gods/sons, then a third lower region with twelve powers/images and two triads of pillars (one structural, one as ‘garments’). Many fills are therefore constrained by correspondential structure (triads/quaternities; boundary/sea; pillars/garments; porter/gates) but exact wording remains uncertain in multiple places; several reconstructions are best-effort substrate-register restorations rather than tight restorations from surviving letters.
